about.text: Brie de Meaux is a French brie cheese of the Brie region and a designated AOC product since 1980. Its name comes from the town of Meaux in the Brie region. As of 2003, 6,774 tonnes were produced annually.

how.label: layer with pelle
how.text: The firm rennet curd is hardly cut and is laid by hand in thin layers into very wide, flat moulds with the perforated pelle à brie, so it drains slowly on its own. The rind ripens the wide, thin wheel from the outside in, turning it from chalky to supple with cream, butter and hazelnut notes after 6–8 weeks.
